text: There are two main types of debt cycles: the short-term business cycle, which lasts 5-8 years, and the long-term debt cycle, which peaks every 50-75 years when debt burdens become unsustainably large relative to incomes.
source: Ray Dalio — How the Economic Machine Works
author: Ray Dalio

text: In a deleveraging, people cut spending, incomes fall, credit disappears, and asset prices drop. Unlike a standard recession, lowering interest rates doesn't work because they are already near zero, rendering traditional monetary policy ineffective.
source: Ray Dalio — Principles for Navigating Big Debt Crises
author: Ray Dalio

text: An all-weather portfolio is balanced based on risk, not dollar amounts, to perform across the four economic environments: rising growth, falling growth, rising inflation, and falling inflation. By balancing risk parity, the portfolio survives regardless of structural shifts.
source: Ray Dalio — Principles for Navigating Big Debt Crises
author: Ray Dalio

text: When short-term interest rates hit zero, central banks must turn to printing money and buying financial assets, commonly known as quantitative easing. This drives up asset prices but exacerbates wealth inequality.
source: Ray Dalio — How the Economic Machine Works
author: Ray Dalio

text: A 'beautiful deleveraging' occurs when policymakers successfully balance deflationary forces (debt restructuring and austerity) with inflationary forces (money printing), keeping the economy stable and allowing nominal growth to exceed interest rates.
source: Ray Dalio — Principles for Navigating Big Debt Crises
author: Ray Dalio
